I have a degree in computer science with fifty years of experience in various positions from computer aided design of computers to teaching people about relational database programming. In that time I have seen computing go through several revolutions, but it seems to me that each revolution is the same thing going on at a different level. I started the level where programming was a singular process - create a program to capture one piece of data and convert it to another piece of data, such as hours worked into a paycheck. Then we started collecting paycheck data along with other company data to create bookkeeping systems. The next step was full accounting systems with connections to outside vendors, at the very least sending tapes of data to our bank to pay the IRS, SSA, employees, insurance, etc. The we created enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems out of the accounting systems inventory to foretell inventory demand based upon sales, vendor lists, cost of goods sold, etc. Networks allowed for a multi-site enterprise to use ERP to make efficient prognostication models. Big data came along with sophisticated statistical models to predict with increased accuracy and efficiency logistics. Remember this all started with a payroll check. Along with this came more humane user interfaces - the easier it became to use these new levels of our business models the complexity of the code became impossible to keep using old languages. So we have languages that rely heavily on complex libraries like Python where the coding looks relatively simple, but what would take hundreds of thousands of lines of code in something like Fortran. I don’t doubt that AI might take my job, but I just need to keep up with the next level of technology to keep doing next level tasks.

Top companies: Data Scientists means scientists (with PhD) For instance, bioinformatics scientist will be hired as Data Scientist, a statistician/mathematician will be hired as Data Scientist. Job description gives details. These data scientist are actually scientists (who have research background), are highly skilled, and capable of working on novel research ideas. Other companies: Data Scientists (bootcamp scientist) are name-only. These so called "scientists" have no research background. Most of these data scientists are either software developers who knows to use some ML library, data analyst, or a BS/MS-level statistician with some programming background. They may have done some kaggle projects and are capable of developing a web apps/dashboards. I don't like to consider these bootcamp scientist as scientist just because they have learned few ML libraries and solve Kaggle problems. Scientist is a person who works on research projects in order to create new knowledge and publish papers following scientific methodology. A person can be a scientist without a degree but his work should fit into this basic definition at least.

I agree with mostly everything you said in about the present and near future situation of ai. Where my take diverges would be the hole in your argument that ai will just stay at its current state and not improve. This is obviously untrue because of the proven scaling laws and the progress it’s already seen with these scaling laws. Eventually If you like it or not ai will be able to do anything a human can with ease. Humans are not that special and we are definitely not the smartest animals to ever exist. Ai is targeting the brain function of a human and beyond. This means that once it rapidly flys by human intelligence level it will be able to do anything…and I mean anything better than a human( mentally and physically). Mentally because of increasing intelligence which is responsible for mental tasks. Physical because humans are the ones designing the robots in the first place…for now. Once ai gets passed the human intelligence segment it will be able to improve the hardware and software of any robot for any purpose. So, you are right in the short term, you are most definitely missing a major piece of the truth which is that ai will continue to improve (in all ways). Recursive self improvement is very real.
